text.p: HSBC James Capel has called for a strong buy on Singapore property and hotels group City Developments Ltd (CityDev) as it has calculated that the group's prospective net asset value (NAV) per share is Singapore $18.40.
In a 60-page report on CityDev released in early April, James Capel said the NAV for CityDev would rise "thanks to the applied imagination" of the Kwek family which controls the company.
The report said CityDev's "balance sheet is full of hidden value" and "the single largest source of NAV growth is reinvestment of the huge cashflows from development properties".
James Capel said a change in government policy last year to release more land for private housing would benefit developers.
It noted that CityDev already had a large landbank of about six million sq ft of freehold land which should be sufficient for the group's development needs over the next five years.
"If CityDev moves more into 99-year leasehold properties which it is slowly doing, it will benefit from the increase in volume," it said.
CityDev's earnings would also broaden with its expansion plans for its investment property portfolio and diversification into other businesses such as infrastructure and healthcare.
It said contributions from the group's hotel arm, CDL Hotels International, was also expected to rise.
CityDev shares were down 40 cents to S$13.70 in late trading on Wednesday.
